Anomaly detector using ARIMA (ARIMA++)

Source: R/hanr_arima.R
hanr_arima.Rd

Fits an ARIMA model to the series and flags observations with large model residuals as anomalies.

Usage

hanr_arima(auto = "aicc", max_order = 12, cv_folds = 2, horizon = NULL)

Arguments

auto

Order selector forwarded to tspredit::fit_arima(): "aicc" (default, compact AICc search) or "cv" (the heavier ARIMA++ rolling-origin cross-validated selector, tuned for forecasting).

max_order

Cap for the ACF/PACF-driven candidate lags (ARIMA++ "cv").

cv_folds

Number of rolling origins for the CV selection (ARIMA++ "cv").

horizon

CV horizon (ARIMA++ "cv"); NULL -> the detected seasonal period.

Value

hanr_arima object.

Details

This is the backport of the Python pyharbinger::HanrArima releitura. Instead of forecast::auto.arima, the ARIMA order is selected by the DAL ARIMA auto-selector tspredit::fit_arima() – the native (base stats::arima) replacement for auto.arima – so harbinger no longer depends on the forecast package. auto = "aicc" (default) is a compact AICc search; the detector flags points whose in-sample ARIMA residual is unusually large.

The first sw_size = max(p, d + 1, q) residuals are a warm-up window: they are neutralised before the outlier statistics (not only masked afterwards), so a large initialisation transient cannot inflate the threshold and hide the real anomalies. Residual magnitudes are summarised via a distance function and thresholded with the outlier heuristics from harutils().

References

  • Box GEP, Jenkins GM, Reinsel GC, Ljung GM (2015). Time Series Analysis: Forecasting and Control. Wiley.

  • Hyndman RJ, Khandakar Y (2008). Automatic time series forecasting: the forecast package for R. Journal of Statistical Software, 27(3). doi:10.18637/jss.v027.i03

Examples

library(daltoolbox)

# Load anomaly example data
data(examples_anomalies)

# Use a simple example
dataset <- examples_anomalies$simple
head(dataset)
#>       serie event
#> 1 1.0000000 FALSE
#> 2 0.9689124 FALSE
#> 3 0.8775826 FALSE
#> 4 0.7316889 FALSE
#> 5 0.5403023 FALSE
#> 6 0.3153224 FALSE

# Configure ARIMA anomaly detector
model <- hanr_arima()

# Fit the model
model <- fit(model, dataset$serie)

# Run detection
detection <- detect(model, dataset$serie)

# Show detected anomalies
print(detection[(detection$event),])
#>    idx event    type
#> 50  50  TRUE anomaly
